# Decision context and model structure

We apply a probabilistic decision model to assess whether large garment
factories in Hanoi, Vietnam should invest in supporting on-site
vegetable access for their workers. Two intervention options are
evaluated against a *DoNothing* baseline:

- **FarmStand**: The company establishes and manages an on-campus
  vegetable stand, sourcing directly from contracted farmers. The
  company bears full establishment and annual operating costs but
  retains control over supply chain quality, worker access, and pricing.
- **ConnectFarm**: The company facilitates connections between workers
  and off-site farming cooperatives, enabling direct purchasing without
  managing a physical stand. Establishment costs are a small fraction of
  FarmStand costs, but the company has less control over quality and
  access reliability.
- **DoNothing**: No intervention. Workers rely on existing off-campus
  food sources. This serves as the counterfactual baseline.

The model evaluates each option in terms of its net financial benefit to
the company over a five-year horizon as the Net Present Value (NPV) of
the intervention *relative to DoNothing*. A positive NPV indicates that
the intervention generates more value (or avoids more cost) than taking
no action. All outputs are probability distributions, reflecting full
propagation of uncertainty across all input parameters.

# Monte Carlo simulation

We parameterised the model using expert-elicited ranges representing the
5th and 95th percentiles of each uncertain input (see Section 3, Table
1). Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 model runs was performed using
the `decisionSupport` R package (Luedeling et al. 2021), drawing
independent samples from each input distribution per run. Costs and
benefits are inflated annually using the `inflation_rate` parameter. All
future cash flows are discounted to Net Present Value using the
`discount_rate`.

Decision outcome variables:

- `decision_farmstand`: NPV of FarmStand minus NPV of DoNothing (million
  VND, discounted over five years)
- `decision_connectFarm`: NPV of ConnectFarm minus NPV of DoNothing
  (million VND, discounted over five years)

```{r mcsimulation, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
source("company_model.R")

# Fixed seed ensures reproducibility across full simulation runs
set.seed(84)

source("functions/mcSimulation.R")
company_simulation_results <- mcSimulation(
  estimate = estimate_read_csv("data/company_input.csv"),
  model_function = company_model,
  numberOfModelRuns = 10000,
  functionSyntax = "plainNames"
)
```

# Input parameters

Table 1 lists all model input variables with their expert-elicited
uncertainty ranges. **Lower** and **upper** bounds represent the 5th and
95th percentiles of each parameter distribution. Distribution types:
*pos-normal* = truncated normal constrained to positive values;
*trunc-normal [0,1]* = normal truncated to the unit interval (used for
probabilities and fractions); *constant* = fixed value.

```{r parameter_table, echo=FALSE}
input_raw <- read.csv("data/company_input.csv", check.names = FALSE)

# Strip trailing/leading whitespace from all column names, then name the blank separator column
names(input_raw) <- trimws(names(input_raw))
names(input_raw)[names(input_raw) == ""] <- "drop"

param_table <- input_raw %>%
  select(variable,
         lower,
         upper,
         distribution,
         label,
         description) %>%
  filter(!is.na(variable), trimws(variable) != "") %>%
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      variable %in% c("number_of_years", "discount_rate", "CV_value",
                       "inflation_rate", "chance_benefit_farmer_revenue") ~
        "Economic and model parameters",
      str_starts(variable, "cost_of_establishment") |
        str_starts(variable, "cost_establishment") ~
        "One-time establishment costs (million VND)",
      str_starts(variable, "cost_of_maintaining") ~
        "Annual maintaining costs (million VND)",
      variable %in% c("connectFarm_meeting_fraction", "connectFarm_promo_fraction",
                       "connectFarm_establishment_fraction",
                       "connectFarm_accessibility_multiplier") ~
        "ConnectFarm scaling parameters",
      str_starts(variable, "benefit_") | str_starts(variable, "base_") |
        variable == "benefit_worker_time_savings" |
        variable == "benefit_farmer_revenue" |
        variable %in% c("prob_increased_farmer_reputation",
                          "health_response_to_food_env") ~
        "Benefit parameters (million VND/yr)",
      variable %in% c("conflicting_business_interests",
                       "revenue_reduction_if_conflicting_interest",
                       "chance_conflict_farmer_buyer",
                       "chance_conflict_farmer_company",
                       "chance_rumor", "relationship_reduction") |
        str_starts(variable, "access_reduction") |
        variable %in% c("disease_outbreak", "change_of_source_undesirable",
                          "chance_low_affordability",
                          "chance_poorly_organized_inconvenient",
                          "chance_not_meet_preference",
                          "reduction_nutrition_low_diverse_and_quality") ~
        "Risk parameters (probabilities and reductions)",
      str_starts(variable, "reduction_in_veg") |
        str_starts(variable, "farming_practice") |
        str_starts(variable, "connectFarm_quality") |
        str_starts(variable, "connect_farming") |
        str_starts(variable, "no_farmstand") |
        str_starts(variable, "do_nothing") |
        str_starts(variable, "chance_vegetable") ~
        "Food quality parameters",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    lower = as.numeric(lower),
    upper = as.numeric(upper),
    distribution = recode(distribution,
      "posnorm"   = "pos-normal",
      "tnorm_0_1" = "trunc-normal [0,1]",
      "const"     = "constant"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(category, levels = c(
    "Economic and model parameters",
    "One-time establishment costs (million VND)",
    "Annual maintaining costs (million VND)",
    "ConnectFarm scaling parameters",
    "Benefit parameters (million VND/yr)",
    "Risk parameters (probabilities and reductions)",
    "Food quality parameters",
    "Other"
  ))) %>%
  select(category, label, lower, upper, distribution, description)

param_table %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "category") %>%
  cols_label(
    label        = "Parameter",
    lower        = "5th %ile",
    upper        = "95th %ile",
    distribution = "Distribution",
    description  = "Description"
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title    = "Table 1. Model input parameters",
    subtitle = "Expert-elicited 5th and 95th percentile ranges for all uncertain inputs"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(lower, upper), decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_style(
    style     = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_row_groups()
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style     = cell_text(size = "small", color = "gray30"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = description)
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size              = "small",
    row_group.background.color   = "#eef2f7",
    column_labels.font.weight    = "bold",
    heading.title.font.size      = "medium",
    heading.subtitle.font.size   = "small"
  )
```

# Simulation results

## Net Present Value distributions

The distributions below show projected NPV for each intervention
relative to DoNothing over five years. Values above zero indicate a net
benefit. Boxes show the interquartile range; whiskers extend to the 5th
and 95th percentiles.

```{r plot_dist_boxplot, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
source("functions/plot_distributions.R")
Fig_distributions <- plot_distributions(
  mcSimulation_object = company_simulation_results, 
  vars      = c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm"),
  old_names = c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm"),
  new_names = c("NPV FarmStand vs. DoNothing", "NPV ConnectFarm vs. DoNothing"),
  method         = "boxplot", 
  base_size      = 11,
  x_axis_name    = "Comparative NPV over five years (million VND)")
Fig_distributions
ggsave("figures/Fig_distributions.png", width = 15, height = 8, units = "cm") 
```

```{r summary_decisions, echo=TRUE}
# Summary statistics for both decision outcomes
summary(company_simulation_results$y[1:2])

# 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles
quantile(company_simulation_results$y$decision_farmstand,  probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
quantile(company_simulation_results$y$decision_connectFarm, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

Table of the NPV positive run-percentage across all 10,000 model runs
realtive to DoNothing.

```{r summary_of_npv_vars_sim_runs_greater_than_zero}

npv_vars <- c(
  FarmStand = "decision_farmstand",
  ConnectFarm = "decision_connectFarm"
)

npv <- company_simulation_results$y[, unname(npv_vars), drop = FALSE]

valid_runs <- vapply(npv, function(x) sum(!is.na(x)), integer(1))
positive_runs <- vapply(npv, function(x) sum(x > 0, na.rm = TRUE), integer(1))

# the positive-run percentage

data.frame(
  scenario = names(npv_vars),
  simulations = valid_runs,
  positive_runs = positive_runs,
  positive_percent = round(100 * positive_runs / valid_runs, 1)
)

```

## Annual cash flows

Annual projected cash flows for each scenario across all Monte Carlo
runs. The orange crossbar marks the median. Year 1 FarmStand costs are
higher due to one-time establishment expenditure.

```{r combined_cashflow_boxplot, message=FALSE}
company_data <- as.data.frame(company_simulation_results$y)

cashflow_farmstand <- company_data %>%
  select(starts_with("cashflow_farmstand")) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Year", values_to = "CashFlow") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(str_extract(Year, "\\d+")), Scenario = "FarmStand")

cashflow_connectFarm <- company_data %>%
  select(starts_with("cashflow_connectFarm")) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Year", values_to = "CashFlow") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(str_extract(Year, "\\d+")), Scenario = "ConnectFarm")

combined_cashflow <- bind_rows(cashflow_farmstand, cashflow_connectFarm)

ggplot(combined_cashflow, aes(x = factor(Year), y = CashFlow, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.color = "gray40", outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.65,
               color = "orange", fatten = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Cash flow (million VND)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ConnectFarm" = "steelblue",
                                "FarmStand"   = "forestgreen")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave("figures/Fig_cashflow_combined_boxplot.png", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r summary_cashflow, echo=TRUE}
cat("--- FarmStand annual cash flows ---\n")
summary(company_simulation_results$y[3:7])
cat("\n--- ConnectFarm annual cash flows ---\n")
summary(company_simulation_results$y[8:12])
```

# Sensitivity analysis (PLS)

We use Projection to Latent Structures (PLS) regression (fitted with the
orthogonal scores algorithm via `pls::plsr`) to identify which input
variables have the strongest influence on each NPV outcome and in which
direction. Variables are ranked by their Variable Importance in
Projection (VIP) score; only variables with VIP \> 0.9 are shown. Bar
colour indicates the direction of the standardised PLS coefficient:
positive (blue) values increase NPV; negative (red) values decrease NPV.

```{r pls_farmstand}
input_table <- read.csv("data/company_input.csv")

source("functions/pls_model.R")
source("functions/plot_pls.R")

pls_result <- pls_model(object     = company_simulation_results,
                        resultName = names(company_simulation_results$y)[1],
                        ncomp      = 1)

plot_pls_farmstand <- plot_pls(plsrResults = pls_result, 
                               input_table = input_table, 
                               threshold   = 0.9) + 
  theme(legend.position  = "none",
        axis.title.x     = element_blank(), 
        axis.text.x      = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks       = element_blank()) + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) + 
  ggtitle("Projection to Latent Structures (PLS)") + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 5, y = 2, label = "FarmStand")

pls_result_connect <- pls_model(object     = company_simulation_results,
                                resultName = names(company_simulation_results$y)[2],
                                ncomp      = 1)

plot_pls_connect <- plot_pls(plsrResults = pls_result_connect, 
                             input_table = input_table, 
                             threshold   = 0.9) + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 5, y = 2, label = "ConnectFarm")

Fig_pls <- plot_pls_farmstand / plot_pls_connect 
ggsave("figures/Fig_pls.png", width = 10, height = 4)
Fig_pls
```

# Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI)

The Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI) quantifies the maximum
a decision-maker should rationally invest to eliminate uncertainty about
a given input variable before making the decision. High EVPI identifies
variables where targeted data collection would most change or reinforce
the decision. EVPI is estimated using LOESS-smoothed empirical curves
across the Monte Carlo sample, parallelised across all input variables
for efficiency.

```{r mc_table, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
mcSimulation_table <- data.frame(company_simulation_results$x, 
                                 company_simulation_results$y[1:2])
npvs_to_move <- c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm")
mcSimulation_table <- mcSimulation_table %>%
  select(-all_of(npvs_to_move), all_of(npvs_to_move))
```

```{r evpi-general_calc, echo=TRUE}
# source("functions/multi_EVPI.R")
# 
# evpi <- multi_EVPI(mc = mcSimulation_table,
#                    first_out_var = "decision_farmstand",
#                    n_cores  = parallel::detectCores() - 1,
#                    mc_samples = 3000)   # subsampled for speed; EVPI stable at n = 3000
# save(evpi, file = "data/data_evpi.Rda")
load("data/data_evpi.Rda")
```

```{r plot_evpi, fig.cap="Figure: EVPI for FarmStand (top) and ConnectFarm (bottom). Only variables above the EVPI threshold are shown. Values represent the maximum investment (million VND) justified to obtain perfect information about each variable."}
source("functions/plot_evpi.R")

plot_evpi_farmstand <- plot_evpi(
  EVPIresults   = evpi,
  decision_vars = "decision_farmstand",
  new_names     = "FarmStand",
  input_table   = input_table,
  threshold     = 10, 
  min_evpi      = 0.005) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 9))

plot_evpi_connectfarm <- plot_evpi(
  EVPIresults   = evpi,
  decision_vars = "decision_connectFarm",
  new_names     = "ConnectFarm",
  input_table   = input_table,
  threshold     = 10, 
  min_evpi      = 0.000001) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 9))

Fig_evpi <- plot_evpi_farmstand / plot_evpi_connectfarm 
ggsave("figures/Fig_evpi.png", width = 20, height = 10, units = "cm")
Fig_evpi
```

# Food environment outcomes

The food environment score aggregates the effects of each intervention
on workers' access to safe, nutritious, and diverse vegetables,
estimated as a productivity-equivalent monetary value (million VND/yr).
The score is computed relative to DoNothing.

```{r plot_food_env, fig.cap="Figure: Distribution of food environment scores for FarmStand and ConnectFarm relative to DoNothing."}
Fig_food_env <- plot_distributions(
  mcSimulation_object = company_simulation_results, 
  vars      = c("farmstand_food_env_score", "connect_food_env_score"),
  old_names = c("farmstand_food_env_score", "connect_food_env_score"),
  new_names = c("Food env. score FarmStand vs. DoNothing",
                "Food env. score ConnectFarm vs. DoNothing"),
  method      = "boxplot", 
  base_size   = 11, 
  x_axis_name = "Comparative food environment score (million VND/yr productivity equivalent)")

Fig_food_env
ggsave("figures/Fig_plot_boxplot_health_food_env.png", width = 25, height = 8, units = "cm")
```

```{r summary_food_env, echo=TRUE}
summary(company_simulation_results$y[13:14])
```

The modeled food-environment score difference relative to DoNothing.

```{r food_env_score_diff_relative_to_do_nothing}

y <- company_simulation_results$y

summarize_scenario <- function(food_var, npv_var, scenario) {
  d <- data.frame(food = y[[food_var]], npv = y[[npv_var]])
  d <- d[complete.cases(d), ]

  data.frame(
    scenario = scenario,
    food_score_positive_pct = 100 * mean(d$food > 0),
    positive_when_npv_positive_pct =
      100 * mean(d$food[d$npv > 0] > 0),
    positive_when_npv_nonpositive_pct =
      100 * mean(d$food[d$npv <= 0] > 0)
  )
}

rbind(
  summarize_scenario("farmstand_food_env_score", "decision_farmstand", "FarmStand"),
  summarize_scenario("connect_food_env_score", "decision_connectFarm", "ConnectFarm")
)
```

# Code and data availability

All model code, input data, and analysis scripts are archived at:

<https://github.com/sau140288/nifam_favri_companies>

The model is implemented in R using the `decisionSupport` package. Monte
Carlo simulation, PLS sensitivity analysis, and EVPI are all fully
reproducible from the code above with `set.seed(84)`.

**Reference:** Luedeling E, Goehring L, Schiffers K, Whitney C,
Fernandez E (2021). *decisionSupport: Quantitative Support of Decision
Making under Uncertainty*. R package version 1.111.
<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=decisionSupport>

Whitney C, Luu TTG, Kopton J, Luedeling E. A decision-analysis framework
for school garden investments in Vietnam: evaluating trade-offs for
nutrition, biodiversity, and economic outcomes. Humanit Soc Sci Commun.
2026;13(1):580. <https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-026-07204-0>
